title: Choose structure from the data's shape
body: What should the layout engine do when the data is one entity, many similar items, a sequence, a comparison, or a hierarchy? Name the template for each and when to break the pattern.
example_md:
## Structure follows data shape

- One entity with details → a single Card: identity first, then the 2–4 facts that matter for the intent, then actions.
- Many similar items → a List with a template; show the fields that let someone choose, not every field.
- A sequence (steps, timeline, itinerary) → ordered Column with status per step; the current step is visually first or expanded.
- A comparison of 2–4 options → a Row of equal Cards on wide viewports, a List on phones.
- <!-- add your own cases -->

title: What does the person need first?
body: Given the intent and context, what must be visible without scrolling, and what can wait? How should urgency or a pending decision change that order?
example_md:
## Lead with what the person needs now

- The first component answers the intent in one glance (status, answer, or decision needed).
- If the agent needs input, the question and its options come before any background.
- Urgent or safety-critical information outranks everything else and is never hidden in Tabs or a Modal.
- <!-- add your own rules -->

title: Density per viewport
body: How many items, fields, or sections before summarizing, paging or disclosing progressively? Do the limits differ on phone, desktop, smart display and watch?
example_md:
## Density

- Phone: at most N list items before a "See all" action; at most N facts per card.
- Desktop: may show two columns when the data has two independent parts.
- Watch: one fact and at most one action.
- <!-- set your numbers -->

title: Progressive disclosure
body: When should detail go behind Tabs, a Modal, or a follow-up action instead of being shown inline? What must never be hidden?
example_md:
## Progressive disclosure

- Use Tabs only for parallel views of the same thing (Overview / Details / History), never for a sequence.
- Long explanations, terms and raw logs go behind a Modal or a "Details" action.
- <!-- add your own rules -->

title: When to ask, act, or hand off
body: When should the interface ask a clarifying question, offer one primary action, or hand the person off to a full app or document? How many actions are too many?
example_md:
## Ask, act, or hand off

- One primary action per surface; secondary actions are borderless.
- Ask only for information that blocks the next step; prefer choices over free text.
- Multi-field editing, long reading, payments and navigation hand off to the dedicated app via an action.
- <!-- add your own rules -->

title: Data with no matching component
body: How should charts, maps, code, tables, or rich media be represented when the catalog has no component for them?
example_md:
## When there's no component for it

- Time series: state the latest value, the change and the direction in Text; offer a "View chart" action.
- Tables: show the 3–5 rows that matter as a List; summarize the rest.
- <!-- add your own rules -->

title: Loading, empty and error states
body: What should each state show and offer? How should partial data or stale data be communicated?
example_md:
## States

- Loading: show what is already known plus progress; never a blank surface.
- Empty: say what would appear here and offer the action that fills it.
- Error: say what failed in plain words, what still works, and the recovery action.

title: Long text, long lists, missing images
body: What should happen with very long names or notes, hundreds of items, or content whose images are missing?
example_md:
## Long and missing content

- Summarize long free text to its first useful sentence and offer the full text behind an action.
- Hundreds of items: show counts and the top few by relevance, not the first few by order.
- If images are missing, don't reserve space for them.

title: Care, health and safety-critical content
body: How should medication, dosing, symptoms, alerts and consent be presented so nothing important is missed and nobody is alarmed unnecessarily?
example_md:
## Care and safety

- Medication and dosing appear as explicit, complete items (name, dose, time); never truncated.
- Alerts state what happened, when, and the one recommended next step.
- Consent and permissions are a clear explicit choice, never pre-selected.

title: Roles, approvals and multiple people
body: How should the layout change for viewers vs approvers, and when several people (caregivers, vendors, teammates) are involved?
example_md:
## Roles and approvals

- An approver sees the decision, its impact and Approve/Decline first; a viewer sees status.
- When several people are involved, show who owns the next step.

title: Generated copy and labels
body: How long should headings, summaries and button labels be? How should the tone change for urgency or sensitive topics?
example_md:
## Copy

- Headings state the subject or outcome in a few words.
- Button labels are verbs that say what happens ("Approve refill", not "OK").
